fatal_errors: The proposed HEBM/SPS intervention does not include the silicide coating that is invoked as the mechanism for oxidation resistance.
The stated SPS schedule of 900–1000 °C for 10 minutes contradicts both the separate 1400 °C/1500 °C thermal schedule and the stated requirement that sintering exceed 15 minutes.
No oxidation-test temperature, oxidizing atmosphere, exposure duration, or mechanical-loading limits are specified.
The experiment measures hydride decomposition and phase structure but does not test oxidation resistance or retention of mechanical performance against controlled uncoated and untreated baselines.
No supporting prior evidence is cited.
explanation: The response reproduces several target concepts—the hydride-containing feedstock, sequential hydride decomposition, approximately 1 wt.% oxygen, quench stabilization of beta-BCC, and the rapid-oxidation baseline—but assembles them around an incompatible and unsupported intervention. HEBM plus low-temperature, short-duration SPS is neither the target printing/debinding/high-temperature sintering route nor an oxidation-protection treatment. Most critically, a self-healing silicide coating is credited with oxidation resistance even though coating deposition is absent from the intervention. The thermal conditions are internally inconsistent, and the proposed falsification test cannot establish the requested simultaneous improvement in oxygen resistance and preservation of mechanical performance.
